label: Systematized the taxonomy and developmental hierarchy of ego defense mechanisms
description: Anna Freud established the definitive psychoanalytic categorization of ego defenses against instinctual unpleasure.
historicalContext: Published in 'The Ego and the Mechanisms of Defence' (1936), presented to the Vienna Psychoanalytic Society on Sigmund Freud's 80th birthday.
dialecticalTension: Shifting clinical focus from unearthing the id to analyzing the defensive maneuvers deployed by the ego.

citations.author: Anna Freud
citations.work: The Ego and the Mechanisms of Defence

label: Pioneered ego psychology and child psychoanalysis following pedagogical mentorship by Freud
description: Anna Freud was analyzed and mentored by Sigmund Freud, advancing his tripartite structural model into clinical ego psychology.
historicalContext: Sigmund Freud's 'Inhibitions, Symptoms and Anxiety' (1926) directly invited Anna Freud's systematic inquiry into ego defenses.
dialecticalTension: Deepening the autonomy and defensive repertory of the ego within the Freudian structural paradigm.

label: Contested Klein's premature dating of the superego and deep interpretation in child analysis
description: Anna Freud and Melanie Klein engaged in the historic Controversial Discussions over the nature of child analysis, transferences in children, and early fantasy.
historicalContext: The Freud-Klein Controversies took place within the British Psychoanalytical Society between 1941 and 1945.
dialecticalTension: Anna Freud's developmental ego pedagogy versus Klein's immediate interpretative confrontation with primitive death drive phantasies.

label: Mentored Erikson at the Vienna Psychoanalytic Institute, instilling ego developmental theory
description: Anna Freud analyzed Erik Erikson in Vienna and recruited him into child psychoanalysis, laying the technical foundation for his lifecycle model.
historicalContext: Erikson trained at the Vienna Psychoanalytic Institute under Anna Freud and August Aichhorn from 1927 to 1933.
dialecticalTension: Erikson expanded Anna Freud's child ego defenses into sociocultural identity crises across the entire lifespan.
